law: A product requires user, job, outcome and harmed-party evidence.
A bounded context requires a coherent local model, language and explicit translations.
Processes, cases, decisions, states and exceptions require fitting behavioral formalisms.
Decision rights, trust boundaries, approvals and effects must be independently modeled.
Aggregate and protocol seams require atomicity, concurrency, safety and liveness evidence.
Composable libraries require commonality, variation points, constraints and binding phases.
Modules, containers, dependencies and ports require a separate implementation view.
Operated products/providers require SLO, capacity, failure, recovery and support evidence.
Independent products/providers require usage, cost, value and exit evidence.
Claimed boundaries must survive observed work, code, logs, data usage, incidents and adversarial cases.
Analytical products require method, data, assumptions, uncertainty and result-authority boundaries.
Hardware, software, people, procedures, requirements and safety constraints require end-to-end traceability.
